newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end quiet day narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end quiet day narrowly mixed.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended narrowly mixed, with most recovering from early losses to end midrange.

September Treasury bond futures initially rallied on a rise in the latest weekly jobless claims to hit a fresh four-month high, then sold off after a strong Philadelphia Federal Reserve business index.
During the afternoon, most debt futures drifted up from the day's lows in quiet trading.
June Treasury bond futures expired quietly at midday, settling down 5/32 to 112-12/32.
Trading was light on the afternoon foray from the lows.
"I would just say we had what might be typical shortcovering," said Kurt Fraim, futures analyst with Aubrey G. Lanston. "It was another quiet day overall."

Technicians said the market was prone to consolidation because September had turned overbought during the recent rally. They pegged resistance at 112-16/32 and 112-28/32. The year's high lurks at 113-9/32, set February 18.
Support was seen at 111-16/32. One technician said a breach of support there would set the market on track for 110-15/32.
John Kadich, futures floor analyst with Dean Witter, said an afternoon rally in U.S. stocks underpinned the light-volume debt futures market.
"That helped us drag it back up a bit," Kadich said. He noted resistance at 112-15/32 and 112-22/32 to 23/32. He said a breach of support at 111-19/32 could spell more losses.
"But for now it looks like we're going to grind sideways to slightly higher," Kadich said.
Still, "even though we have a bullish tone, without a correction any upside is going to be hindered without any bullish news," he added.
The early push to a new four-month high was tied to the unexpected 8,000 rise in jobless claims to 347,000.

Also early in the session, it was reported that the U.S trade gap widened to $8.36 billion in April, well below forecasts for a $10.0 billion deficit and compared to a downwardly revised $7.76 billion in March.
Later, Philadelphia Fed's business activity index rose to 25.2 in June from 1.6 in May, knocking debt futures to session lows.

At the close, September T-bonds were up 1/32 at 112-6/32, December Eurodollars were down 0.010 pt to 93.95, and 10-year notes were down 3/32 at 108-31/32. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
